provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Plants we eat
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list plants we eat
The pupils should be able to sort vegetables into roots stems and leaves

Introduction:
We eat different plant parts. Some plants grow in our market.

Content:
Roots we eat are carrot yam and potato. Stems we eat are sugarcane and bamboo. Leaves we eat are spinach and cabbage. We can eat roots stems or leaves of plants.

Class activity:
Bring real carrots potatoes spinach cabbage. Let pupils touch and sort them into roots stems and leaves.

Evaluation questions:
Name one root we eat. Name one stem we eat. Name one leaf we eat. Which part of plant do you like most?

Summary:
We eat different parts of plants like roots stems and leaves.

topics.title: Grow our food
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to plant maize and beans
The pupils should be able to state steps for planting seeds

Introduction:
Food comes from plants. We can grow food ourselves.

Content:
Growing food needs soil water and sun. First dig a small hole. Put seed in hole. Cover seed with soil. Water the seed daily. Wait for it to grow.

Class activity:
Each pupil plants a maize or bean seed in a cup. Make a roster for watering duty.

Evaluation questions:
What do plants need to grow? What is first step for planting? What is second step? Who will water today?

Summary:
We can grow our own food by planting seeds and caring for them.

topics.title: Soil types
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify sandy clay and loam soil
The pupils should be able to sort soil samples

Introduction:
Soil helps plants grow. Different soil types feel different.

Content:
Sandy soil feels rough and dry. Clay soil feels sticky when wet. Loam soil feels soft and good for plants. Good soil helps plants grow strong.

Class activity:
Give pupils samples of sandy clay and loam soil. Let them feel each type and sort them into correct groups.

Evaluation questions:
How does sandy soil feel? How does clay soil feel? Which soil is best for plants? How do we know?

Summary:
There are three main soil types sandy clay and loam.

topics.title: Small creatures big jobs
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state how worms help plants
The pupils should be able to identify bees as plant helpers

Introduction:
Small animals help plants in big ways. Worms and bees are helpers.

Content:
Worms make soil soft and rich for plants. Bees help plants make fruits by moving pollen. Without these helpers plants would not grow well.

Class activity:
Make a simple wormery with soil and worms. Let pupils observe how worms move through soil.

Evaluation questions:
What do worms do to soil? What do bees do for plants? Name one plant helper. How do they help?

Summary:
Small creatures like worms and bees help plants grow.

topics.title: Bird watch
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to name local birds
The pupils should be able to identify bird nests

Introduction:
Birds are flying animals around us. They build homes in trees.

Content:
Common local birds are pigeon hawk and weaver bird. Birds make nests from twigs grass and mud. Nests are where birds lay eggs and keep babies safe.

Class activity:
Make simple binoculars from paper rolls. Take class outside to watch birds and look for nests in trees.

Evaluation questions:
Name one bird you see. What is a nest? What do birds use to build nests? Where do birds live?

Summary:
Birds build nests in trees and help control insects.

topics.title: Animal classification
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to sort animals into farm wild and water
The pupils should be able to name examples of each group

Introduction:
Animals live in different places. We can group them by where they live.

Content:
Farm animals are cow goat and chicken. Wild animals live in forest or bush like lion and squirrel. Water animals live in rivers or sea like fish and crab.

Class activity:
Give pupils pictures of different animals. Let them sort them into farm wild and water groups.

Evaluation questions:
Name one farm animal. Name one wild animal. Name one water animal. Where does a lion live?

Summary:
Animals can be grouped as farm wild or water animals.

topics.title: Body movement science
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to point to joints and muscles
The pupils should be able to demonstrate different movements

Introduction:
Our body moves with parts called joints and muscles.

Content:
Joints are where two bones meet like knee and elbow. Muscles help us move and bend. Without joints and muscles we could not walk or play.

Class activity:
Play robot game where pupils move like stiff robots then stretch like rubber to show how joints and muscles work.

Evaluation questions:
Where is your knee joint? What do muscles do? How do you bend your arm? What happens if you have no joints?

Summary:
Joints and muscles help us move our body.

topics.title: Senses experiment
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify taste smell and touch
The pupils should be able to describe objects using senses

Introduction:
We use our body to learn about things around us.

Content:
Our tongue helps us taste sweet salty bitter. Our nose helps us smell good and bad things. Our hands help us feel rough smooth or soft.

Class activity:
Set up three stations. Taste station with fruits. Smell station with spices. Touch station with different textures. Blindfold pupils and guess.

Evaluation questions:
What do we use to taste? What do we use to smell? What do we use to feel? Can you name something sweet?

Summary:
We use our senses of taste smell and touch to learn about things.

topics.title: Simple machines
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify lever ramp and pulley
The pupils should be able to use simple machines to move objects

Introduction:
Machines help us work easier. Simple machines are lever ramp and pulley.

Content:
A lever is a stick that helps lift heavy things. A ramp is a sloping surface to push things up. A pulley uses rope to pull things up high.

Class activity:
Let pupils use a ruler as lever to lift book. Use a plank as ramp to move toy car. Use pulley to lift small bucket.

Evaluation questions:
What is a lever? What is a ramp? What is a pulley? How do machines help us?

Summary:
Simple machines like lever ramp and pulley help us work easier.

topics.title: Revision and garden harvest
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to share what they learned about growing
The pupils should be able to taste harvested plants

Introduction:
We have learned about plants and growing food. Now we harvest.

Content:
Growing food takes time and care. We planted seeds watered them and watched them grow. Now we can eat what we grew.

Class activity:
Each pupil presents one thing they learned about growing plants. Then harvest and taste simple plants like beans or lettuce.

Evaluation questions:
What did you plant? What did you learn about plants? How do plants grow? How does your plant taste?

Summary:
Growing food is fun and we enjoyed eating what we grew.
